_comment: Provenance for WASM bundles built from the pqctoday-hsm repo and vendored into this hub. When you rebuild a bundle with its hsm build script, update its `hsmCommit`/`builtAt`. Verify drift with `npm run sync:wasm:check` (compares against a sibling ../pqctoday-hsm checkout when present; no-op otherwise). Bundles built from other sources (openssl upstream, pqctoday-tpm) are intentionally omitted.

bundles.name: cacp-kmip
bundles._buildNote: Prior rebuilds (2026-07-10/11, merged via hub #410/#411/#412, hsm #139/#140): corrected a stale manifest entry, picked up CKA_ALLOWED_MECHANISMS/CKO_CERTIFICATE engine-side support, fixed the wasm32 compile break in Register/Import's certificate projection, and added the WP-4 raw_pkcs11_encrypt_probe showcase export. This rebuild (hub #413, merged) adds the WP-3 showcase (`Pkcs11CertificateDemo.tsx`): a real fix (Register(Certificate) with a PublicKeyLink now reuses that key's own CKA_ID instead of minting a fresh one, matching the native Certify path — hsm #141, merged; `hsmCommit` above is that PR's squash-merge commit on hsm main) plus two wasm exports, `register_certificate_demo` and `engine_certificate_attributes`. Verified: native `cargo test -p pqctoday-kmip` (593 passed), wasm32 build + smoke test, and a standalone node script + a real-browser Playwright pass confirming a genuine Register → engine-projection → real CKA_SUBJECT/CKA_ISSUER/CKA_SERIAL_NUMBER/CKA_VALUE readback (not simulated).

bundles.name: softhsmrustv3-engine
bundles._buildNote: PKCS#11 v3.2 Baseline Provider + generic pre-hash mechanisms (2026-07-17, hsm commit 644a839, landed directly on main): adds the CKO_PROFILE object (CKA_PROFILE_ID=CKP_BASELINE_PROVIDER, every Profiles v3.2 §5.1 requirement checked against the fetched spec) and implements the previously-unadvertised generic CKM_HASH_ML_DSA (0x1F) / CKM_HASH_SLH_DSA (0x34) pre-hash mechanisms (CK_HASH_SIGN_ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT.hash parsing, remapped onto the existing hash-specific mechanisms). `hsmCommit` above (5c0eadd) is a same-day follow-up that only refreshes hsm's own tracked rust/pkg_bundler/ build artifact + a wasm/Cargo.lock version bump — no rust/ source changed beyond 644a839. No new exported wasm functions — same API surface (.d.ts/.js text diffs are empty), only the .wasm binary changed; verified 302 Rust unit tests pass (0 failed) and the .wasm binaries are byte-identical across all three hub vendor copies (public/wasm/rust/, src/wasm/, src/vendor/softhsm-wasm/wasm/ — the last of which was found stale relative to the other two, predating the FrodoKEM/McEliece shadow-stack fix, and is now back in sync as a side effect of this rebuild). Prior entry (`5303bd3`, 2026-07-11): fixed the FrodoKEM/Classic-McEliece wasm32 shadow-stack overflow in Encapsulate — see hsm CHANGELOG.md for that history.

bundles.name: softhsm-cpp-engine
bundles._buildNote: Includes fix(cpp) 250994d: SP800-108 KDF now requires keyed-MAC PRF (CKM_SHA256_HMAC); bare hash IDs rejected per PKCS#11 v3.2 §6.42.

bundles.name: openssl-pkcs11
bundles._buildNote: PKCS#11 engine swapped from the C++ SoftHSMv3 fork to the pure-Rust softhsmrustv3 (hsm rust/, wasm32-unknown-emscripten staticlib). The C++ fork's only crypto backend is OpenSSL libcrypto -- the same libcrypto.a linked into this binary -- so the chain CLI -> pkcs11-provider -> C++ softhsm -> same libcrypto was circular. The Rust engine has no OpenSSL dependency (RustCrypto + patched fips204/205/ml-kem), making the provider path a genuinely independent implementation. Also in this build: -sSTACK_SIZE=8MB (Emscripten's 64KB default overflows during ML-DSA/ML-KEM keygen and traps with 'memory access out of bounds'); pkcs11-provider config.h is now generated by scripts/gen-pkcs11-provider-config-h.sh rather than required to pre-exist, and defines DEFAULT_PKCS11_MODULE so the provider resolves the in-process engine with no config file; the apps_startup() provider-registration patch ('Fix A') is recovered into pqctoday-priv/openssl-wasm-patches/ after previously existing only inside a gitignored openssl source tree. Verified in Node against the real binary: provider loads and reports the Rust engine, C_InitToken/C_InitPIN/C_GenerateKeyPair(ML-DSA-65) succeed, token state survives a full snapshot -> fresh-module -> restore cycle, and the CLI reads the key back through a pkcs11: URI as a real PUBLIC KEY PEM. Pinned anchor KATs (ML-DSA-44/65/87, SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s, ML-KEM-512/768/1024 decap + bit-flip negatives) pass against this binary.
